description:
Upstream handles xterm-style modified CSI sequences: `\e[1;2A` (Shift+Up), `\e[1;5A` (Ctrl+Up), `\e[1;3A` (Alt+Up), and the same pattern for B/C/D (arrows), H/F (Home/End), P-S (F1-F4), and `\e[N;modM~` for modified F5-F12/Insert/Delete/PageUp/PageDown.

Our legacy_csi parser has no handling for the `;mod` parameter in CSI sequences. This means Shift+Up, Ctrl+Down, Alt+Right, etc. all return `:unknown` when the terminal uses xterm-style reporting (which is the default for most terminals when Kitty protocol is not active).

This is a critical gap — it breaks Ctrl+Left/Right word navigation and Shift+Enter newline insertion in terminals that report these as CSI sequences rather than legacy escape codes.

Implement: in `legacy_csi/1`, detect the `<num>;<mod><final>` pattern and parse the modifier bits (same bitmask as Kitty: shift=2, alt=3, ctrl=5, etc., where the reported value is modifier+1).

Ref: `keys.ts` L609-624 (arrow match), L387-411 (general CSI modifier parsing).
title: KeyParser: xterm modified CSI sequences (\e[1;modA for Shift/Ctrl/Alt+arrows and nav keys)
